newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds push forward in line with German bunds.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds push forward in line with German bunds.

text.p: Irish bonds continued to push forward in thin late trade on Wednesday in line with German bunds which have out-performed U.S. Treasuries, dealers said.

Dealers said Treasuries were held up slightly after U.S. business inventories in November rose only 0.1 percent versus a forecasted rise of 0.3 percent while German analysts were saying bunds should go higher.
"The States has slipped back a bit today while Germany opened strong and continued to push ahead on the back of good bid interest," one dealer said.
"We have also seen good two-way bid interest in Irish bonds. Spreads against German bunds have come in. Irish bonds should match any further gains made in Germany," the dealer added.

By 1630 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had gained 30 pence from Tuesday's close at 102.40 to yield 5.82 percent while the benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 had risen 45 pence from the close at 109.75 to yield 6.48 percent.

Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at 160 basis points over German bunds in the five-year-area, versus 172 late last week. Irish bonds were trading at 86 basis points over bunds in the 10-year-area versus 95 on Friday.

A close eye will be kept on U.S. jobless claims data due out at 1330 GMT and the Philadelphia Fed index survey due out at 1500 GMT on Thursday for clues as to whether or not a rise in U.S. rates is imminent.
